title: The Empty Ambulance
narration: An ambulance arrived for me before I called for help. Its dashboard counted down as an allergic reaction tightened my chest. Inside, an injection carried my name, and the doors locked. My business partner followed with a remote controller after increasing my life insurance. Police stopped him when I escaped. Doctors examined the labelled medicine. The silence felt deliberate, as though someone nearby was waiting for me to understand the trap before moving again. For several seconds I could hear nothing except my breathing and the small ordinary sounds around me. Every explanation I tried made the details worse, because each clue had been placed where I alone would find it. I wanted to leave immediately, but doing that would mean abandoning the only proof that any of this had happened. It contained the allergen; the countdown measured how long he expected me to resist taking it.
